question: How strongly do the selected texts justify restrictions on demonstrations on public-order grounds?

custom_lens.name: Public-order framing in the Civic Square hearing

criteria.label: Documented safety risk
criteria.description: The source explicitly cites a record or measurement of concrete emergency-access harm, such as a documented ambulance delay. A proposed risk, a reference to an available traffic plan, or a call for future measurements by itself does not meet this criterion.

criteria.label: Favorable appraisal of restrictions
criteria.description: The source favorably characterizes the proposed two-block exclusion zone as a safety or public-order measure. A negative appraisal, neutral mention, or quoting an opponent's language without endorsement does not meet this criterion.

criteria.label: Restriction as remedy
criteria.description: The source recommends adopting the proposed two-block exclusion zone to address a safety or public-order problem. Recommendations limited to emergency lanes, stewards, or data collection do not meet this criterion.

criteria.label: Prior controls presumed ineffective
criteria.description: The text presents failure of existing controls as a taken-for-granted premise of the proposed measure. If wording such as restore order lacks a clear connection to a specific prior control or is explicitly questioned, preserve uncertainty.
